page: Microsoft Azure DS13_v2 is a DSv2-family virtual machine running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 8 dedicated physical cores and 8 vCPUs powered by an Intel Xeon 8272CL x86_64 processor operating at 2.6 GHz. The processor includes 32 KB of L1d cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 35 MB of L3 cache. It supports key instruction sets such as AVX, AVX-512F, AES, BMI2, ADX, and FMA, though it lacks newer extensions like AVX-512 VNNI or AMX. The instance is configured with 56.0 GB of system memory, yielding 7.0 GB of RAM per core, and includes 115 GB of local storage. No GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses are bundled with this instance.

Performance benchmarks position the DS13_v2 primarily in the average tier for multi-core and memory operations, while single-core capabilities are relatively weak. The single-core stress-ng score of 1356.49 and Geekbench single-core score of 1085.0 fall into the bottom 25% of tested hardware. Similarly, single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression show lower-tier performance. Conversely, multi-core execution is more robust, with a Geekbench multi-core score of 5978.0 and a stress-ng multi-core score of 10830.52 placing it in the middle 50%. Memory bandwidth is stable, reaching 720.03 GB/sec for cached small blocks and 76.69 GB/sec for uncached large blocks.

With its high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 7.0 GB per core, the DS13_v2 offers a balanced profile for memory-intensive workloads that do not demand cutting-edge single-threaded CPU speeds. It achieves average performance in database operations, with a Passmark database score of 4601.14 and 11.85 million operations per second in Redis SET benchmarks. Static web serving throughput is measured at 9.93 GB/sec. The instance is suitable for relational databases, caching layers, software compilation, and light text or image processing. However, it is less efficient for heavy single-threaded tasks or large-scale LLM inference, as demonstrated by its weak performance on 7B parameter models.
